name: De Vinne 14pt 1897
designer: Unidentified in the retained source pages
foundry: Shown by the United States Government Printing Office; 1897 stock mark Keystone–10
description: Fourteen-point De Vinne with flared serifs, a sweeping Q tail, double-storey a and g, and observed mixed-height figures. Six named alternates retain source variations.
character_set_notes: Complete observed A–Z, a–z and ten figures, with period, comma and the double-bar historical hyphen encoded as hyphen-minus. Space has a modern layout advance. Six observed alternatives are unencoded glyphs available through stylistic sets; no unsupported character is inferred. Nine whole observed diagonal fractions, cent and percent are also encoded. Fraction row-center placement is a modern layout convention, independent of historical baseline evidence.
observed: The 1897 specimen supplies both complete fourteen-point alphabets. Matching census and job-room impressions supply clearer letters, all ten figures and punctuation. The census M and five differently shaped or positioned figures are retained as named alternatives. The census ten-figure row is the default set; its unequal positions are preserved. Matching ATF assortments supply whole 14-point diagonal fractions and symbols; exact selected pages, crops, thresholds and scale measurements are retained.
reconstructed: No visible form is invented. Uniform source-page scaling, measured rigid baseline rotation, local paper correction and modern spacing prepare the observed forms. No cross-size substitution or independent width stretching. One measured two-pixel enclosed printing pinhole in B is cleaned without changing the outer contour or intended counters. Fraction row-center placement at350 is a modern layout choice; no historical text baseline is established by the charts. No fraction parts are assembled or redrawn.

revival.notes: All visible forms are observed. A uniform scale per physical source page and measured rigid baseline rotations preserve optical proportions. Six named alternatives are exposed through ss01/ss02/ss03. The numeral block has its own measured baseline on the gently bowed scan line. See source/METHOD.md for reproduction and feature use. The whole fraction companions retain their full physical source dimensions and deliberate slash interruptions. Existing outlines, spacing and named alternatives are preserved.
